questions.q: How does a user account most commonly come to exist in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: It is purchased separately from the application
It is automatically created when a worker record is created
Every user account must be typed in manually by Oracle support
It is generated the first time someone tries to sign in
questions.explain: In most implementations, user account auto-creation triggers the moment a worker record (such as a new hire) is created.

questions.q: A newly created user account for a new hire at Castellan Robotics has not yet been provisioned any roles. What can that user do when they sign in?
options: Everything in the system, by default
Only what General Ledger allows
Essentially nothing — a user account carries no access on its own
Only reporting, never transactions
questions.explain: A user account by itself carries no access. Access only exists once roles are provisioned to the account, which is covered in Lesson 9.

questions.q: What distinguishes a 'locked' account from an 'inactive' account?
options: There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
Locked is a temporary state usually from failed sign-in attempts; inactive means the account cannot sign in at all, typically after termination
Inactive accounts can still run reports; locked accounts cannot
Locked accounts have more access than inactive ones
questions.explain: Locked is typically a temporary lockout from repeated failed sign-ins, cleared by an admin or password reset. Inactive is a deliberate deactivation, often tied to termination.

questions.q: Which task is used to search for a user, view account status, or deactivate an account?
options: Manage Users
Manage Bank Accounts
Create Journal Entries
Define Data Access Sets
questions.explain: Manage Users, found in the Security Console, is the task administrators use to maintain user accounts.

questions.q: Why does promptly deactivating a terminated employee's user account matter beyond basic tidiness?
options: It has no real importance
It frees up a software license slot only
An active account tied to someone who should no longer have access is a gap that security audits specifically look for
It automatically deletes that employee's historical transactions
questions.explain: Leaving a terminated employee's account active is exactly the kind of access gap that security reports and audits, covered in Lesson 14, are designed to catch.
